title: BastionBlueprintBundle
description: v1 BASTION battlefield blueprint compile of AuthoringWorld. Independent of SimulationBundle: separate wire, separate decoder, separate schema file (human call 2026-09-15, CD-91 D.4 key bastion_blueprint_bundle). SimulationBundle's 22 bags and to_dictionary() are byte-identical to before M6, because TRAPRUSH's ContentHash covers that wire and published content plus old replays hang off it. Two explicit discriminators up front: schema_version and gameplay. The blueprint input is still a plain AuthoringDocument and Component Schema v1 is unchanged; roles are declared with zone.tags and fields borrow v1 components (see game/src/ugc/bastion_blueprint_compiler.gd). This wire carries no tower or unit numbers: damage, health, speed and bounty are placeholder stubs in game/src/games/bastion/play_stubs.gd while CD-63 §1.2 / §1.3 stay deferred. Economy scalars are here because CD-22 §7.1 makes them creator-editable. Prototype ids are the M6 minimum set only (three towers, three units, three obstacles); the wider CD-22 candidate tables are explicitly not locked and must not be added here without a human call. Waypoint node ids are derived by the compiler, ascending, and edges are strictly ordered by (from_id, to_id) so one blueprint has exactly one wire form. Unsigned wire. Platform signatures are the ContentSign sidecar. Not Rule VM.

team_id.description: 1v1 has exactly two teams. Multi-team and 2v2 belong to M7; this wire keeps no extension slot because an unverified slot is worse than none.

tower_prototype_id.description: M6 minimum tower set: arrow, cannon, frost. Sniper / arc / amplifier from CD-22 §5.1 are candidates, not M6. Kept in sync with game/src/ugc/bastion_prototype_catalog.gd by tools/content-validator/src/gdscript_sync.ts.

unit_prototype_id.description: M6 minimum unit set: swift, heavy, swarm. Shield / support / boss from CD-22 §5.2 are candidates, not M6.

obstacle_prototype_id.description: M6 minimum obstacle set: barricade, slow tile, diverter. Shield pylon / jammer pad / fog zone from CD-22 §4.2 are candidates, not M6.

core.description: One per team. Position is not duplicated here; node_id points into waypoints. Both sides must declare the same max_health (CD-22 §2 fairness).

build_slot.description: Towers never stand on a lane cell, so a build slot carries its own position instead of a node_id.

obstacle_slot.description: Must sit on a lane node of its own team, otherwise placing an obstacle there cannot change any path.

edge.description: Directed, integer cost in lane cells. Both endpoints must exist and belong to the same team.

wave.description: One shared table for both teams. Mirrored waves are fair because there is only one table, not because two tables are compared (CD-22 §5.2).

economy.description: Exactly these eight scalars. Creator-editable per CD-22 §7.1, which is why they travel in the wire instead of living in the placeholder stubs.
